### What is Research?

.three-col[
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("compass", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**A Journey of Discovery**

Research is a systematic investigation to establish facts and reach new conclusions.
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**Question-Driven**

Every great discovery begins with a well-framed question that guides your direction.
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**Evidence-Based**

Research relies on gathering and analyzing evidence rather than opinions or assumptions.
]
]


---
class: center, middle

<br>

## Sports Analytics: Do Home Teams Really Win More?

.font130[**Do home teams have a real advantage in the NBA &mdash; and if so, _why_?**]

--

.three-col[
.col[
.content-box-blue[
**The Fan's Opinion**

"Of course they do! The home crowd fires up the players and rattles the visitors."
]
]
.col[
.content-box-blue[
**An Analyst's Hypothesis**

Maybe it isn't the crowd at all &mdash; it could be travel fatigue, familiar rims, or favorable refereeing.
]
]
.col[
.content-box-blue[
**A Research Approach**

Pull every NBA game from basketball-reference.com, compare home vs. away win rates, then test _which_ story the evidence supports.
]
]
]

---
## What the NBA Data Shows

.pull-left[
```{r nba-home, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, cache=FALSE, out.width="100%", out.height="430px", fig.width=8, fig.height=6, fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Real NBA regular-season home win % (basketball-reference.com / NBA.com)
nba_home <- tibble::tribble(
  ~season,        ~home_win_pct,
  "2000–13 avg",  60,
  "2014–19 avg",  58,
  "2020–21",      54,
  "2022–23",      58,
  "2023–25 avg",  54
)
nba_home$season <- factor(nba_home$season, levels = nba_home$season)

ggplot(nba_home, aes(x = season, y = home_win_pct)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#0148A4", width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(home_win_pct, "%")), vjust = -0.6, size = 6,
            family = "firasans") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.6, y = 51.5, label = "50% = no advantage",
           hjust = 0, colour = "#D55E00", size = 5, family = "firasans") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 68)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Home team win %",
       title = "Home teams win more than half their games") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 13))
```
]

.pull-right[
.font110[Across two decades, NBA home teams have won **well above 50%** of regular-season games &mdash; but the edge has **shrunk over time**.]

#### `r fontawesome::fa("trophy", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; ~60% home wins in 2000&ndash;2013

#### `r fontawesome::fa("arrow-trend-down", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Down to ~54% in recent seasons

#### `r fontawesome::fa("user-slash", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Lowest (54%) in 2020&ndash;21 &mdash; **empty arenas**
]

---
## So... is this a research question?

.three-col[
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**Is this a research question?**

"Home teams win more" is a _fact_. "_Why_ do they win more?" is the research question.
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass-chart", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**What evidence would we need?**

Crowd size, travel distance, rest days, referee calls &mdash; data that can separate the competing explanations.
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("scale-balanced", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**What would 'prove' it?**

We don't "prove" &mdash; we build evidence. The **empty-arena 2020&ndash;21 season** acts like a natural experiment on the crowd effect.
]
]

### From Curiosity to Focused Questions

.three-col[
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("bolt", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**Curiosity Spark**

The urge to know more about something that intrigues you.
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("cloud", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**Wonder**

Asking yourself "Why is this happening?" or "How does this work?"
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**Research Question**

Transforming curiosity into a clear, specific question to explore.
]
]

### A Key Attitude of a Researcher: Inquisition

<br>

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[**"How do I know that?"**]

.content-box-blue[**"What information is this opinion based on?"**]

.content-box-blue[**"What's that claim based on?"**]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-blue[**"Has anyone actually tested it?"**]

.content-box-blue[**"Where is the evidence?"**]
]

### Questioning Claims: The Mozart Effect

.font80[
<div class="chev-flow">
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("quote-left", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>The Claim</strong><br>
    "Listening to classical music while studying guarantees an A on the test."</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("question", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>The Inquiry</strong><br>
    "What's that claim based on? Has anyone actually tested it?"</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>The Research</strong><br>
    Find scientific studies or conduct a small experiment comparing study methods.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("chart-line", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>The Evidence</strong><br>
    Music may help mood or focus for some people, but doesn't "guarantee" success.</p>
  </div>
</div>
]

### Core Principles of Good Research

#### <span style="color:#0148A4;">No matter what the field is</span>

--

<div style="position:relative; width:540px; height:380px; margin:0.2em auto 0 auto;">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 420 330" width="540" height="380" preserveAspectRatio="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
    <polygon points="210,0 280,110 140,110" fill="#0148A4"/>
    <polygon points="143.8,116 276.2,116 340,216 80,216" fill="#7fb8e0"/>
    <polygon points="83.5,222 336.5,222 405,330 15,330" fill="#c9e4f6"/>
  </svg>
  <div style="position:absolute; top:63px; left:270px; transform:translate(-50%,-50%);">`r fontawesome::fa("handshake", height = "1.4em", fill = "#ffffff")`</div>
  <div style="position:absolute; top:104px; left:270px; transform:translate(-50%,-50%); color:#ffffff; font-weight:bold;">Be Honest</div>
  <div style="position:absolute; top:173px; left:270px; transform:translate(-50%,-50%);">`r fontawesome::fa("list-check", height = "1.4em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
  <div style="position:absolute; top:213px; left:270px; transform:translate(-50%,-50%); color:#0148A4; font-weight:bold;">Be Systematic</div>
  <div style="position:absolute; top:297px; left:270px; transform:translate(-50%,-50%);">`r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass", height = "1.4em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
  <div style="position:absolute; top:337px; left:270px; transform:translate(-50%,-50%); color:#0148A4; font-weight:bold;">Be Curious</div>
</div>

---
### Principle 1: Be Curious

.pull-left[
```{r img12, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="75%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/12-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("bolt", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; The Starting Point
Curiosity is where all research begins&mdash;the spark that ignites investigation.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Everyday Questions
Major discoveries often begin with simple observations or moments of wonder.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("door-open", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Embracing the Unknown
Being comfortable asking "Why?" and "What if?" drives meaningful research.
]

---
### Principle 2: Be Systematic

.pull-left[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("route", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Beyond Hunches
Systematic research follows clear procedures rather than random exploration.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("rotate", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Replicability
Others should be able to follow your process and reach similar conclusions.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("folder-open", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Organization
Keeping careful records and following methodical steps builds credibility.
]

.pull-right[
```{r img13, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="75%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/13-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

---
background-image: url("assets/13a-strip.png")
background-position: 50% 80%
background-size: 90%

### Principle 3: Be Honest

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("file-lines", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Report All Findings**

Include inconvenient results that don't match your expectations.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Accept Uncertainty**

Acknowledge when the data doesn't show clear answers.
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("quote-right", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Give Credit**

Cite sources properly and acknowledge others' contributions.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("handshake", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Build Trust**

Integrity makes your research valuable in school and beyond.
]
]

---
### The Value of Being Wrong

.pull-left[
```{r img14, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/14-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("face-surprise", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Embrace Unexpected Results
Surprising findings often lead to the most important discoveries in research.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("graduation-cap", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Learning Opportunity
When your hypothesis is wrong, you've learned something valuable about what isn't true.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("shield-halved", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Intellectual Honesty
Acknowledging incorrect assumptions demonstrates scientific integrity and builds credibility.
]

---
### The Research Process

.font110[The journey from question to insight follows these essential steps:]

.font80[
<div class="chev-flow">
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>1. Ask a Question</strong><br>
    Formulate a clear, specific question worth investigating.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>2. Gather Information</strong><br>
    Collect relevant data through appropriate methods.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("chart-line", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>3. Analyze the Information</strong><br>
    Examine data for patterns, trends, and meaning.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>4. Draw Conclusions</strong><br>
    Develop evidence-based answers to your original question.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("share-nodes", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>5. Share Findings</strong><br>
    Communicate results effectively to appropriate audiences.</p>
  </div>
</div>
]

### Real Research Example: AI Art in Education

.pull-left[
```{r img14a, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=4, fig.height=6, out.width="58%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/14a-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[.font80[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Question**

Could AI tools help more students feel empowered to create art?
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Information Gathering**

Surveys, teacher interviews, examples from other schools, literature review.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("chart-line", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Analysis**

30% felt confident in drawing skills; 80% would try AI art tools.
]

.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Conclusion & Action**

AI art competition could broaden creative access; school launched pilot program.
]
]]

---
### Case Study: School Lunch Research

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", fill = "#4a7fb5")` The Question**

Layla wondered: Are students getting nutritious lunches that support focus and learning?
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Hypothesis**

Students avoid lunches due to taste, freshness, or variety issues&mdash;not lack of hunger.
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("clipboard-list", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Research Design**

- **Quantitative:** Lunch program participation data
- **Qualitative:** Student surveys and focus groups
- **Observational:** Cafeteria behavior patterns
- **Stakeholder:** Staff interviews
]
]

---
### Lunch Research: Findings and Impact

.pull-left[
```{r img15a, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=4, fig.height=6, out.width="58%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/15a-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[.font80[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass-chart", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Key Findings**

Students wanted fresher options, menu variety, and customization.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Solutions Proposed**

Student advisory panel, taste tests, nutritional labeling, diverse options.
]

.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("chart-line", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Results**

School piloted ideas; lunch participation and satisfaction increased.
]

.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("graduation-cap", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Lesson**

Research can solve real problems and improve everyday experiences.
]
]]

---
### Summary: Key Takeaways

.pull-left[
```{r img14b, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=4, fig.height=6, out.width="58%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[.font80[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("book", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Research Definition**

Systematic investigation to answer questions using evidence.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("scale-balanced", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Opinion vs. Evidence**

Research moves beyond personal beliefs to factual conclusions.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("layer-group", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Research Types**

Scientific, social science, historical, and interdisciplinary approaches.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("route", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Research Process**

Question, gather, analyze, conclude, and share findings.
]
]]

class: segue-yellow

# Let's Play a Game: <br> FACT (research-supported) <br> or MYTH (misconception)? `r top_icon("gamepad")`

---
class: center, middle

.font130["The current global warming trend is primarily caused by natural climate cycles, not human activity."]

--

.font110[`r fontawesome::fa("xmark", fill = "#D55E00")` **MYTH** &mdash; Research shows over **97% of climate scientists** agree that human activities&mdash;mainly burning fossil fuels&mdash;are the primary cause of current global warming. *(NASA, 2024 &ndash; climate.nasa.gov/evidence)*]

---
class: center, middle

.font130["As of 2024, more than half of the global population lives in urban areas rather than rural ones."]

--

.font110[`r fontawesome::fa("check", fill = "#009E73")` **FACT** &mdash; Over 56% of people worldwide live in urban settings, a number projected to reach 70% by 2050. *(United Nations, 2024 &ndash; un.org/development/desa/publications)*]

---
class: center, middle

.font130["Studies show that renewable sources like wind and solar could theoretically meet 100% of global energy needs."]

--

.font110[`r fontawesome::fa("check", fill = "#009E73")` **FACT** &mdash; Research suggests a full transition to renewables is technically feasible, though it would require major investment and infrastructure changes. *(Jacobson et al., 2017 &ndash; Joule, 1(1), 108&ndash;121)*]

---
class: center, middle

.font130["Mental health problems are mostly caused by personal weakness or a lack of willpower."]

--

.font110[`r fontawesome::fa("xmark", fill = "#D55E00")` **MYTH** &mdash; Mental health conditions are caused by a mix of biological, psychological, and environmental factors, not personal failure. Willpower alone cannot prevent or cure mental illness. *(National Institute of Mental Health, 2024)*]

---
class: center, middle

.font130["Most people without access to safely managed drinking water live in sub-Saharan Africa."]

--

.font110[`r fontawesome::fa("check", fill = "#009E73")` **FACT** &mdash; Nearly 400 million people in sub-Saharan Africa lack safely managed water, making it the most affected region. *(WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme, 2023 &ndash; washdata.org)*]

---
class: center, middle

.font130["Biodiversity loss only affects wildlife and has little impact on human life."]

--

.font110[`r fontawesome::fa("xmark", fill = "#D55E00")` **MYTH** &mdash; Biodiversity loss disrupts food systems, disease regulation, and clean air/water, directly impacting human survival. *(IPBES Global Assessment Report, 2019)*]

---
class: center, middle

.font130["AI makes fair decisions because it doesn't have feelings or emotions like humans."]

--

.font110[`r fontawesome::fa("xmark", fill = "#D55E00")` **MYTH** &mdash; AI systems can **reproduce bias** if the data or design reflects human inequality. Lack of emotion doesn't equal fairness. *(MIT Media Lab, 2019 &ndash; gender-shades.org; Nature, 2020)*]

---
class: center, middle

.font130["Over half the world's school-aged children are out of school."]

--

.font110[`r fontawesome::fa("xmark", fill = "#D55E00")` **MYTH** &mdash; In reality, about 244 million children and youth are out of school&mdash;roughly 12%, not over 50%. *(UNESCO, 2023)*]

---
class: center, middle

.font130["Vaccines can help stop pandemics, but only if a large percentage of the population receives them."]

--

.font110[`r fontawesome::fa("check", fill = "#009E73")` **FACT** &mdash; High vaccination coverage is needed for herd immunity to protect both individuals and communities. *(World Health Organization, 2022)*]
